changeDirectives.humanReadableDescription: Update the constants file to define configurations for different attachment types (Images, PDFs, Documents, etc.) and to add new DOM selectors needed for filtering.

logic: 1. Create and export a new object constant named 'ATTACHMENT_TYPE_CONFIG'. This object will be the single source of truth for all attachment-specific filtering.
2. Populate 'ATTACHMENT_TYPE_CONFIG' with keys for the new filter categories: 'IMAGE', 'PDF', 'DOCUMENT', 'SPREADSHEET', and 'PRESENTATION'.
3. The value for each key must be an object with the following structure:
- 'extensions': An array of lowercase file extension strings (e.g., ['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif']).

- 'gdriveIdentifier': A string used to identify Google Drive files of this type. This string will be looked for in the 'src' attribute of the attachment icon's '' tag (e.g., 'document' for Google Docs).
- 'icon': The name of the Material Icon to use for the filter button (e.g., 'image').
- 'labelKey': The internationalisation (i18n) key for the button's text label (e.g., 'button_filter_images').
4. In the existing 'SELECTORS' object, add two new key-value pairs:

- 'attachmentRow: 'div.brd'': This selector identifies the container element for attachments within an email row. Note: If this selector fails, the code should also check for the second 'div' inside the parent 'td' as a fallback.
- 'attachmentChip: 'div.brc'': This selector identifies each individual attachment 'chip' within the attachment row.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the file is imported, when 'ATTACHMENT_TYPE_CONFIG.IMAGE.icon' is accessed, then it must return 'image'.
Given the file is imported, when 'ATTACHMENT_TYPE_CONFIG.DOCUMENT.gdriveIdentifier' is accessed, then it must return 'document'.
Given the file is imported, when 'SELECTORS.attachmentRow' is accessed, then it must return 'div.brd'.
Given the file is imported, when 'SELECTORS.attachmentChip' is accessed, then it must return 'div.brc'.

changeDirectives.humanReadableDescription: Add internationalisation (i18n) keys and their English translations for the new attachment filter buttons to the 'en' locale file.

logic: 1. Add new JSON keys for each new attachment filter button: 'button_filter_images', 'button_filter_pdfs', 'button_filter_documents', 'button_filter_spreadsheets', and 'button_filter_presentations'.
2. The value for each new key must be an object with a single 'message' property.
3. The 'message' property's value should be the English text for the button's tooltip and accessible label (e.g., 'Images Only', 'PDFs Only', 'Documents Only').
acceptanceCriteria: Given the JSON is parsed, when the value for key 'button_filter_images' is accessed, then it must be an object '{ "message": "Images Only" }'.
Given the JSON is parsed, when the value for key 'button_filter_documents' is accessed, then it must be an object '{ "message": "Documents Only" }'.

changeDirectives.humanReadableDescription: Update the application's state management to include the new attachment filter modes, so the app knows they are valid filter options.

logic: 1. Locate the 'FILTER_MODES' array, which defines all valid filter states for the application.
2. Append the new mode keys as strings: 'IMAGE', 'PDF', 'DOCUMENT', 'SPREADSHEET', 'PRESENTATION'.
3. These strings must exactly match the keys defined in 'ATTACHMENT_TYPE_CONFIG' in the constants file.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the file is imported, when 'FILTER_MODES.includes("IMAGE")' is checked, then it must return true.
Given the file is imported, when 'FILTER_MODES.length' is checked, then it must be the original length plus 5.

changeDirectives.humanReadableDescription: Implement the core logic for identifying if an email row contains a specific type of attachment (e.g., a PDF, an image). This function will be the brain of the new filtering feature.

inputs.name: row
inputs.description: The DOM element for the entire email row (a '<tr>' element).

inputs.name: attachmentType
inputs.description: The key for the desired attachment type, which must match a key in 'ATTACHMENT_TYPE_CONFIG' (e.g., 'IMAGE', 'PDF').

outputs.description: Returns 'true' if an attachment matching the specified type is found in the row, otherwise returns 'false'.

logic: 1. Within the 'row' element, find all individual attachment chips using the 'SELECTORS.attachmentChip' selector from the constants file.
2. Retrieve the configuration for the requested 'attachmentType' from the 'ATTACHMENT_TYPE_CONFIG' constant.
3. Iterate through each attachment chip found in the row.
4. For each chip, determine if it's a standard attachment or a Google Drive attachment and check if it matches the requested type:

a. **Standard Attachments:** Get the filename from the chip's 'title' attribute. Extract the file extension (the part after the last '.'), convert it to lowercase, and check if this extension is included in the 'extensions' array from the attachment type's config.

b. **Google Drive Attachments:** Check if the chip has a 'data-docurl' attribute containing 'google.com'. If so, find the '' element inside the chip. Get its 'src' attribute. Check if this 'src' string includes the 'gdriveIdentifier' string from the attachment type's config (e.g., includes the word 'presentation').
5. If a match is found by either method, stop iterating and immediately return 'true'.
6. If the loop completes without finding any matches, return 'false'.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a row with an attachment chip having a 'title' of 'report.pdf', when called with attachmentType 'PDF', then it must return true.
Given a row with an attachment chip having a 'title' of 'photo.jpeg', when called with attachmentType 'DOCUMENT', then it must return false.
Given a row with a Google Drive chip whose internal '' has a 'src' containing '...icon_1_spreadsheet.png', when called with attachmentType 'SPREADSHEET', then it must return true.

changeDirectives.humanReadableDescription: Update the main 'applyFilter' function to incorporate the new attachment-specific filtering logic.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: The current filter mode, which could be one of the new attachment modes.

outputs.description: Applies the chosen filter to the DOM by showing or hiding email rows.

logic: 1. Inside the main loop that iterates through each email row ('tr.zA'), add a new conditional block (e.g., an 'else if' or a 'switch' case) to handle the new attachment filter modes.
2. Check if the current 'mode' is one of the keys in 'ATTACHMENT_TYPE_CONFIG'.
3. If it is, the condition to show the row ('showRow') should be: 'hasAttachmentRow(row) && hasSpecificAttachmentType(row, mode)'.
4. This ensures that for a mode like 'PDF', the row is only shown if it both contains attachments in general AND contains a specific PDF attachment.
5. The existing logic for showing/hiding the row based on the 'showRow' boolean remains the same.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the mode is 'PDF', when applyFilter is run, then only email rows containing at least one PDF attachment must be visible.
Given the mode is 'IMAGE', when applyFilter is run, then an email row with only a '.docx' attachment must be hidden.

changeDirectives.humanReadableDescription: Modify the 'createToolbar' function to dynamically generate and add the new filter buttons to the UI.

logic: 1. Import the 'ATTACHMENT_TYPE_CONFIG' object from the constants file.
2. Get the DOM element that acts as the container for the filter buttons.
3. Iterate over the keys of the 'ATTACHMENT_TYPE_CONFIG' object (e.g., 'IMAGE', 'PDF', etc.).
4. For each key, create a new '<button>' element.
5. Use the information from the config object for that key to set the button's properties:
- 'id': `filter-${key}` (e.g., 'filter-IMAGE').
- 'title': Get the translated string using 'chrome.i18n.getMessage(config.labelKey)'.
- 'aria-label': Set to the same translated string as the title.
- Inner HTML: Should contain a '<span>' for the Material Icon, with the icon name set to 'config.icon'.
6. Append each newly created button to the toolbar's button container element, ensuring they appear after the 'Calendar Only' button but before the 'Attachments Only' button for a logical grouping.
acceptanceCriteria: Given createToolbar is called, when the DOM is inspected, then a button with id 'filter-IMAGE' must exist inside the toolbar.
Given createToolbar is called, when the DOM is inspected, then the button with id 'filter-PDF' must have a 'title' attribute with the value 'PDFs Only' (assuming English locale).
Given createToolbar is called, the total number of filter buttons should be the original number plus five.

changeDirectives.humanReadableDescription: Add comprehensive unit tests for the new 'hasSpecificAttachmentType' function to ensure its reliability.

logic: 1. Create several mock HTML row elements using string literals or a DOM manipulation library (like JSDOM, which is already set up).
2. These mocks should represent different scenarios: a row with a standard image, a row with a Google Doc, a row with a mix of attachments, and a row with no relevant attachments.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a mock row containing an attachment chip with 'title="photo.jpg"', when hasSpecificAttachmentType(row, 'IMAGE') is called, then it must return true.
Given a mock row containing an attachment chip with 'title="business-plan.docx"', when hasSpecificAttachmentType(row, 'DOCUMENT') is called, then it must return true.
Given a mock row containing a Google Drive chip with an '' whose 'src' includes 'icon_1_spreadsheet', when hasSpecificAttachmentType(row, 'SPREADSHEET') is called, then it must return true.
Given a mock row containing an attachment chip with 'title="archive.zip"', when hasSpecificAttachmentType(row, 'IMAGE') is called, then it must return false.
Given a mock row with three attachment chips, one of which is 'report.pdf', when hasSpecificAttachmentType(row, 'PDF') is called, then it must return true.

changeDirectives.humanReadableDescription: Add unit tests for the 'createToolbar' function to verify that the new attachment filter buttons are created correctly.

logic: 1. Before running the test, set up a mock for the 'chrome.i18n.getMessage' function to return predictable strings for the button labels (e.g., return 'Images Only' when called with 'button_filter_images').
2. Create a mock DOM element to represent the toolbar container.
3. Call the 'createToolbar' function, passing it the mock container.
4. After the function runs, assert that five new button elements have been added as children to the mock container.

5. Select one of the new buttons (e.g., the one with 'id="filter-SPREADSHEET"') and assert that its 'title' attribute and inner content (the icon) are set to the expected values based on the mocked i18n labels and the constants.
acceptanceCriteria: Given createToolbar is executed on a mock DOM element, when the number of child buttons is counted, then it must equal the original number of buttons plus five.
Given the test setup, the button with id 'filter-PRESENTATION' must have its 'title' attribute set to the mocked i18n value for 'button_filter_presentations'.
